explanation: Pointing with a single finger isn't a serious taboo in France, but it's seen as a bit brusque or childish. French etiquette favors gesturing with an open hand, or a subtle nod or chin lift, to indicate people or objects, especially in polite or formal company.
local_tip: When indicating someone or something, use an open hand or a slight nod rather than a single pointed finger.

also_check.note: Pointing at a person with the index finger is considered quite rude; gesturing with an open hand is the polite alternative.
Pointing is acceptable casually but can read as confrontational or rude in formal settings.
Pointing with the index finger is considered offensive; the thumb or an open hand is used instead.
